You are building the biggest quality gap-closer for Cyrus: a FUNCTIONAL ACCEPTANCE ORACLE. Today eval 'pass' = compiles + boots; the playtest stage is 0/90 run, so we do not know whether a generated mod DOES what the prompt asked (the owner found a goblin mod that compiled and booted but did not even enable). Read /root/CLAUDE.md, /root/claudeskills/memory/MEMORY.md, /root/claudeskills/agent-notes/cyrus-research/BX-improvement-research-2026-10-14.md (card 1 and related), BY-inventory-gaps-2026-10-14.md, CYRUS-TRACKER.md sections 100-111 (Test Flight tf-lite-6, mineflayer survival bot 'stress'/'botMode', goldens, RCON checks, lib/cyrus/testflight/*, scripts/cyrus/golden-flight.ts, eval-run.ts). NEVER edit or build in /opt/nxeon. Worktree: `cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-oracle -b feature/cyrus-behaviour-oracle main`. Tests via scripts/devhost; real flights only on node-2 respecting the shared build lock (see CLAUDE.md / HANDOFF). Commit trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not deploy.

BUILD
1. A declarative 'expectations' schema derived per build from the plan + spec (e.g. command /goblins give exists and gives item X; item with ability triggers on right click and produces particle/effect/damage; menu opens via command with N buttons and clicking slot S runs action; quest objective completes after simulated action; mob spawns via natural/summon and has custom model entity; config key changes behaviour after /reload; recipe is craftable) generated deterministically from designer specs/rig specs/config schema/plugin.yml (no model call required), plus optional model-authored extra expectations kept off by default.
2. An executor inside the existing Test Flight runner (RCON + the mineflayer bot + server log/event probes + inventory/entity queries via RCON `data get`/`execute if`) that evaluates each expectation with an evidence record (pass / fail / not_testable with reason) and a total 'functional score'. Keep flight time bounded (cap +60 s) and failure-isolated: an oracle bug must never fail the plugin (report oracle error as not_run). Apply the 'suspect the oracle' rule: every expectation type has a known-good golden and a mutant (deliberately broken variant) in tests proving it can fail.
3. Integrate: store results in cyrus.testFlight.functional, show a compact 'What we verified' panel in the portal build view (no raw jargon), include in eval-run/eval-journal-stats as the 'behaviour' stage and in the 'real pass' definition if the eval-realism branch (feature/cyrus-eval-realism, another agent) lands first; coordinate by keeping the stage name 'behaviour' and the JSON shape documented in docs.
4. Prove it on real flights: run it against at least 6 existing real build jars (fetch artifacts from the build service GET /builds/<id>/artifact with MODBUILDER_API_KEY from /etc/nxeon/modbuilder.env: use the owner batch builds listed in /root/cyrus-eval/owner-batch-2026-10-14/records.json plus 4 goldens) and report which expectations pass/fail/not_testable, with at least one genuine catch or an honest statement that none were found.
Deliver: branch verified (tsc + new tests + existing testflight tests), docs updated, report /root/claudeskills/agent-notes/cyrus-research/CD-behaviour-oracle-2026-10-14.md with evidence, limits, owner commands (portal promote; does it need an image bump? state).
